description: Feed health, freshness and exporter health across every GBFS system.
title: GBFS feed health

panels.description: Prometheus could not scrape the exporter for this target: the process is down, the port is closed, the scrape timed out, or the exporter answered HTTP 503 because max_in_flight was full. Read this first, because it makes every panel below unreliable.
panels.title: Targets not scraping

panels.description: The exporter answered, but it could not read the operator. Any feed of the system, or the auto-discovery file, failed.
panels.title: Systems with a failed feed

panels.description: How many single feeds failed. A failure of the auto-discovery file counts here as feed="gbfs", and in that case it is the only feed series that the system has.
panels.title: Feeds down

panels.description: Feeds whose data is more than ten times the published ttl old. This is the alert from the README. The auto-discovery file is left out, because it lists the other feeds and changes rarely.

targets.expr:
count(
(time() - max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}))
/ clamp_min(
    max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_ttl_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"})
  or
    (max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}) * 0 + 60)
, 60)
  > 10
)
or (count(gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}) * 0)

panels.title: Stale data feeds

panels.description: The longest single feed read. request_timeout is 10 seconds, so a value near 10 means a read that hung rather than one that failed fast.
panels.title: Slowest feed read

panels.description: Requests that the exporter turned away inside the dashboard range: a bad target, a host outside allowed_hosts, an unknown module, or too many scrapes at once. A restart resets the counter, so watch the restart annotation.
panels.title: Requests refused in range

panels.description: One row per feed that a system publishes. Age and the budget leave out the auto-discovery file, so its freshness cells stay empty on purpose. Read is bounded by request_timeout, which is 10 seconds. The budget is the age divided by ten times the published ttl, so 1.0 means the data just reached the age that the README alerts on.

targets.expr: time() - max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"})

(time() - max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}))
/ clamp_min(
    max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_ttl_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"})
  or
    (max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}) * 0 + 60)
, 60)

panels.title: Data feed ledger

panels.description: Not a data freshness signal. gbfs.json is an index of feed URLs, so its last_updated says when that list changed, not when the data did. Entur serves a Trondheim index six hours old while every feed it lists is under a minute old, and that is correct. Judge staleness in the ledger.
panels.title: Discovery index age

panels.description: The oldest data feed of each system, as a share of ten times its published ttl. The line at 1.0 is where the README alert fires. The auto-discovery file is left out.

targets.expr:
max by (system) (
(time() - max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}))
/ clamp_min(
    max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_ttl_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"})
  or
    (max by (system, feed) (gbfs_feed_last_updated_timestamp_seconds{feed!="gbfs", job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}) * 0 + 60)
, 60)
)

panels.title: Worst data feed staleness

panels.description: Three readings per system, from the outside in. Scraped is whether Prometheus reached the exporter. Read is whether the exporter read every feed the operator publishes. The two differ: the exporter can answer perfectly and still report a broken operator.
panels.title: System state

panels.description: How long Prometheus waited for the whole scrape. The exporter reads the feeds of a system at the same time, so this is close to the slowest feed and not to their sum. The exporter budget is 30 seconds and the scrape timeout is 45.
panels.title: Scrape wall time

panels.description: The longest single feed read per system. request_timeout caps one feed at 10 seconds.
panels.title: Slowest feed in each system

panels.description: The headline numbers of every system side by side, so a figure that cannot be true stands out. Occupancy divides the vehicles at stations by the capacity of the stations that report both, which is the only ratio that holds for a car system reporting no free docks. The disabled columns read "not published" for every operator here, because none publishes the field. A column that reads "not published" is a field the operator withholds, not a fault of the exporter.

targets.expr:
sum by (system) (gbfs_station_vehicles_disabled{job=~"$job", system=~"$system"})
  or (sum by (system) (gbfs_up{job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}) * 0)

sum by (system) (gbfs_station_docks_disabled{job=~"$job", system=~"$system"})
  or (sum by (system) (gbfs_up{job=~"$job", system=~"$system"}) * 0)

panels.title: Per-system totals

panels.description: The build that is answering right now.
panels.title: Build

panels.description: Requests the exporter turned away, by reason, as an exact delta over the dashboard range. bad_target is a missing or malformed target, forbidden_host is a target outside allowed_hosts, unknown_module names a module the file does not hold, and too_many_in_flight means more than max_in_flight scrapes at once.

targets.expr:
sum by (reason) (gbfs_exporter_requests_rejected_total{job="gbfs_exporter"})
  - (sum by (reason) (gbfs_exporter_requests_rejected_total{job="gbfs_exporter"} offset $__range)
     or (sum by (reason) (gbfs_exporter_requests_rejected_total{job="gbfs_exporter"}) * 0))

panels.title: Requests refused, by reason
